record.original_question: Let f1 and f2 ∈ H ∞ (unit disc) = H ∞ ; and let the function g ∈ H ∞ satisfy the inequality |g(z)| ≤ |f1 (z)| + |f2 (z)|. Do there necessarily exist functions g1 and g2 in H ∞ such that g2 = f1 g1 + f2 g2 ? In other words, is it true that g 2 ∈ I(f1 , f2 ) (the ideal generated by f1 and f2 )? Wolff has proved that g3 ∈ I(f1 , f2 ). Also Rao has given an example of a function g∈/ I(f1 , f2 ). For related results by Tolokonnikov, see [381, p. 399]. (J. Garnett)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H^\infty$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, equipped with the supremum norm. Given $f_1, f_2 \in H^\infty$, let $I(f_1, f_2) = \{f_1 h_1 + f_2 h_2 : h_1, h_2 \in H^\infty\}$ denote the ideal of $H^\infty$ generated by $f_1$ and $f_2$.

Suppose $g \in H^\infty$ satisfies the pointwise inequality
$$|g(z)| \le |f_1(z)| + |f_2(z)| \qquad \text{for all } z \in \mathbb{D}.$$

It is known that under this hypothesis $g^3 \in I(f_1, f_2)$, while in general $g$ itself need not lie in $I(f_1, f_2)$.

Question: must $g^2 \in I(f_1, f_2)$? Equivalently, do there always exist $g_1, g_2 \in H^\infty$ such that
$$g(z)^2 = f_1(z)\, g_1(z) + f_2(z)\, g_2(z) \qquad \text{for all } z \in \mathbb{D}\,?$$
artifact.category_tag: Ideals in H^∞ and corona-type theorems
artifact.status_search_result: S. Treil resolved Wolff's $g^2$ problem negatively: there exist $f_1, f_2, g \in H^\infty$ with $|g| \le |f_1|+|f_2|$ on $\mathbb{D}$ for which $g^2 \notin I(f_1,f_2)$. Treil further showed that $g^{1+\varepsilon} \in I(f_1,f_2)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$, so the exponent $2$ is the precise borderline failure between Wolff's $g^3$ result and Rao's counterexample for $g$.

status_evidence.title: Estimates in the corona theorem and ideals of H∞: A problem of T. Wolff (S. Treil)
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves Wolff's question by exhibiting a counterexample showing g^2 need not belong to I(f1,f2), while proving g^{1+ε} ∈ I(f1,f2) for every ε>0.
status_evidence.claim: The g^2 problem of Wolff has a negative answer.

status_evidence.title: Estimates in the corona theorem and ideals of H∞: A problem of T. Wolff, J. Anal. Math.
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of Treil's resolution of Wolff's problem on ideals in H∞.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed publication of the negative resolution.
